For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. It has **2,073.6 Wh of capacity** and a **2,600 W inverter**, giving comfortable headroom for the igniter and an estimated **two or three 12-hour cooks per charge**. It’s also a better fit for a campsite if you’ll be charging other gear. [Dealectric’s runtime and specs](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

For **one cook and a lighter, lower-cost setup**, about **1,000 Wh** should generally do: a pellet grill uses roughly **35–60 W once lit**, with a brief higher draw during ignition. Check your smoker’s startup requirements, and remember that lights or phone charging reduce runtime. [Pellet-grill sizing guide](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)

These estimates are for **pellet grills**, not electric smokers with heating elements, which need substantially more power.
